'''Somdatta Sinha''' (born 1951)<ref name="insaindia">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P09-1496|title=INSA|publisher=Insaindia.org|access-date=11 Jan 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111221034/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P09-1496|archive-date=2014-01-11}}</ref> is an [[Indian people|Indian]] researcher and professor of biology, who is one of the earliest to start working in the area of [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical biology]] in India. Her expertise is in the interdisciplinary fields of mathematical & [[computational biology]], [[nonlinear dynamics]] and [[complex systems]] with a view to understand the logic and design of biological processes. She studies spatio-temporal organization in biological systems – from biological sequences to spread of disease in populations – using mathematical and computational methods. She has played a central role in the development of mathematical and computational biology in her country through research, organization of scientific meetings, training programs, conferences, and teaching interdisciplinary courses at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Her research encompasses patterns, interactions, and dynamics of biological systems using mathematical and physical methods to understand complex multi-scale biological systems. Sinha's research contributions focus on modelling a variety of biological systems, such as, [[circadian rhythm]]s, [[pattern formation]], [[biochemical pathways]], [[synthetic biology]], single and meta-population [[Ecosystem model|ecological models]], [[epidemiology]], and controlling spatiotemporal dynamics. She has also carried out computational analysis of genomes for classification of organisms using Chaos Game Representation (CGR) and [[Multifractal system|Multi-fractal]] analysis, [[protein structure]] function analysis using [[graph theory]], and [[Network analysis (electrical circuits)|network analysis]] of large biochemical pathways. Her publications have made important contributions in the respective fields and are highly cited. Her seminal contribution to the development of the interdisciplinary field of Mathematical and Computational Biology in India was acknowledged by the Department of Biotechnology, Govt of India with the National Senior Woman Bioscientist Award (for life time contribution) in 2013<ref>{{cite web |title=National Senior Woman Bioscientist Award |url=http://dbtindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/NWBAwardeesfrom1999-2016.pdf |website=/dbtindia.gov.in |access-date=2 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230323165847/https://dbtindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/NWBAwardeesfrom1999-2016.pdf |archive-date=Mar 23, 2023 |page=2 |language=en |date=2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> and the J C Bose National Fellowship from the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], Govt. of India.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CCMB scientist gets JC Bose Fellowship|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/hyderabad/2011/oct/20/ccmb-scientist-gets-jc-bose-fellowship-302272.html|access-date=2020-10-02|website=The New Indian Express |date=16 May 2012 }}</ref> She is a fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and [[The National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="ias">{{cite web|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/womeninscience/somdatta.html#85|publisher=Ias.ac.in|title=WiS|access-date=11 Jan 2014}}</ref> She was elected Fellow of the [[Berlin Institute for Advanced Study|Wissenschaftskolleg]] zu Berlin (Institute of Advanced Study at Berlin, Germany) for 2000-2001<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin: Somdatta Sinha, Ph.D.|url=https://www.wiko-berlin.de/en/fellows/academic-year|access-date=2020-10-02|website=Somdatta Sinha, Ph.D.|language=en-US}}</ref> and International Visiting Research Scholar at the [[Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies]] at the [[University of British Columbia]], Vancouver, Canada in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-04-26|title=Somdatta Sinha|url=https://pwias.ubc.ca/profile/somdatta-sinha|access-date=2020-10-02|website=Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies}}</ref> She has traveled widely across the globe and has given many invitational talks in universities and conferences.

She did her school and university (B.Sc. and M.Sc. in [[physics]]) from [[Visva-Bharati University|Visva Bharati University]] and M.Phil. and Ph.D. in [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|theoretical biology]] from [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]], New Delhi (1982). She worked as a scientist at the [[Center for Cellular and Molecular Biology]], Hyderabad, from 1983 to 2011. She then was appointed a full professor and later a visiting professor at [[IISER Mohali|Indian Institute of Science Education and Research]] Mohali (IISER Mohali) <ref name="iisermohali">{{cite web|title=Dr. Somdatta Sinha's Page|url=https://web.iisermohali.ac.in/dept/dbs/?iiser-faculty=somdatta-sinha|access-date=11 January 2014|publisher=Iisermohali.ac.in}}</ref> from 2011 to 2016 and 2016 to 2019. Currently she is the INSA Honorary Senior Scientist at IISER Kolkata,<ref>{{Cite web|title=IISER Kolkata - Honorary Professors|url=https://www.iiserkol.ac.in/web/faculty/honorary-professors#gsc.tab=0|access-date=2020-10-02|website=www.iiserkol.ac.in}}</ref> She has been a visiting professor at the [[Ashoka University]], Sonepat.,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty/Staff|url=https://www.ashoka.edu.in/faculty#!/somdatta-sinha-1632|access-date=2020-10-02|website=Ashoka University|language=en}}</ref> at the Centre for DNA Fingerprinting & Diagnostics (CDFD), and at the Mathematics Department of the University of British Columbia at Vancouver, Canada. She has written many popular science articles in journals and magazines in both English and [[Bengali language|Bengali]], and has co-authored [[NCERT]] science text books.<ref name="blogspot">{{cite web|url=http://ccmbscientists.blogspot.in/2009/01/research-profile-of-somdatta-sinha.html|title=CCMB SCIENTISTS: Research Profile of Somdatta Sinha|date=30 January 2009 |publisher=Ccmbscientists.blogspot.in|access-date=11 Jan 2014}}</ref> In 2024 she was awarded the Sanmarg Aparajita Life time Achievement Jury Award for being a pioneering researcher in theoretical biology in India.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Archives - Aparajita, an initiative by Sanmarg, felicitates women, who have carved a niche for themselves by excelling in their fields of expertise with determination |date=15 March 2024 |url=https://aparajita.sanmarg.in/archives/}}</ref>
